82635886: An OR Gate produces a signal when any of its inputs are active. Find one on the Gadgets page of your Tools Bag, and then use the left stick and action button to select it and place it onto a Microchip.  Attach a switch to each of the OR Gate’s inputs. The OR Gate will light up and produce a signal whenever any – or both – of the switches are activated. No matter which of its inputs are active, the OR Gate will produce a signal. Now hover your popit cursor over the OR Gate and press the menu button to open its tweak menu. From here, you can add more ports using the Number of Ports tweak. Activate the Invert Output tweak to make the OR Gate produce a signal whenever none of its inputs are active, instead. Finally, use the Output Value tweak to change whether the OR Gate produces a signal based on its highest input or whether its signal is based on all its inputs added together. This tweak isn’t important for basic use, though, so don’t worry too much about it!

2908046358: The Dephysicalize Tool is a quick and clean way of removing an object’s physical properties. An object affected by the Dephysicalize Tool cannot be pushed, pulled, or bumped into by anything in the world. This is handy for things like secret walls to walk through, but it’s also worth noting that an object with no physics is cheaper for the game to render, which means that dephysicalizing things that don’t need physics will make your level run better! The tool itself is on the Tools page of the Tools Bag. Select it now and have a look. To dephysicalize something, just point at it with the cursor and press the action button. See how it fades out? That signifies that it has been dephysicalized, but don’t worry – it will only appear this way while you have the Dephysicalize Tool selected. If you change your mind or select the wrong thing, just press the action button again to give it its physics back. When you’re done, just head back to the menu with the back button!

2872132282: The Popit Cursor is your key to Create! Open the popit menu with the menu button, then select the Popit Cursor with the action button.  There it is! The Popit Cursor. The Popit Cursor is also what you use when you want to hook up outputs and inputs in logic. Just hover the cursor over an output and press the action button to grab the wire. Then use the left stick to drag the wire to an input and press the action button again! Now the logic is linked and you’re good to go!  If you want to open an object’s tweak menu, hover the cursor over it and press the menu button. Most things have at least a few tweak options to explore, so tweak everything! Finally, when you’re done with the Popit Cursor, just press the back button to put it away!

4284617674: The Characters Page is where all the characters available to your adventure live. You can find it in your Global Stuff. Right out of the box, you’ll notice the usual suspects: Sackboy, Toggle, Oddsock, and Swoop. But you can add custom characters as well. Once you’ve set up a customised playable character, it needs to be captured. Find the Capture Character option in the Functions tab. Now use the left and right sticks to shape a box around your character and press the action button. And there you have it! Your character is captured and ready to go. Look, there it is on your characters page. We should probably give it a name, so highlight it and press the menu button and change it from the generic name to something a little fancier.  If you want to make a change to your character, you can bring out a fresh copy with the Edit button. Once you’ve made it even better, you’ll need to Recapture it from its character menu. This will refresh every reference to your character throughout your adventure automatically; you don’t need to redo it all! To try your character out, select Transform and have a go! To change back to normal, just select Sackboy on the characters page and hit the action button. Finally, if you decide you don’t need your character anymore, you can delete it! Now you’re ready to fill your adventures with loads of fun characters, new and old!

394066835: Every level begins somewhere! Players enter your levels by popping out of the Entrance, so you should probably know how they work. They’re on the Gameplay page of your Tools Bag, or you can just use the one that comes free with every fresh level! Place one into the world and take a look. Use the left stick and the menu button to enter the Entrance’s tweak menu. Set it to static if you want it to stay in place and then check out the other options. With the Entrance Type tweak, you can determine whether the Entrance is for everyone or for specific teams. You can also set it to Last Activated if you only want it to behave as a Checkpoint for the players who personally activate it. If you want your players to have infinite lives from the very start, activate the Entrance has Infinite Number of Spawns tweak. If your level is part of a larger adventure and you wish for it to have multiple Entrances, that’s no problem at all! Just make the Entrance a Start Point and set up a tag. Then, when you want to send a player back to the level with something like a Scoreboard or a Level Link, just point it the appropriate tag. If you want players to start your level as a specific character, just use the action button to open up your Characters page and select whichever one you like. If you change your mind, just use Reset. Finally, you can tweak the appearance of your Entrance and whether it makes noise to be 100% sure it fits in with your creative vision.

3976200360: With a Mover attached, an object will head off in whichever direction you like. They’re found on the Gadgets page of your Tools Bag. Navigate to them with the left stick and select them with the action button, then place it onto an object using the left stick and the action button. Oh, there it goes! Without a logic signal to tell it otherwise, the Mover defaults to on. It’s probably best to Pause while you set one up. Do so, then open the Mover’s tweak menu using the menu button. The first category of tweaks is the speed category. Use the left stick and the left and right directional buttons to set up the Mover’s Left/Right Speed. Note that a positive number will make the Mover move to the right, and a negative number will make the Mover move left. Similarly, for the Up/Down Speed tweak, a positive number moves up and a negative number moves down. The Local Space tweak changes whether a Mover determines its directions based on the rest of the world – up is always up, left is always left – or whether it determines directions based on the orientation of the Mover.  Next, the strength category! Tweak the Mover’s acceleration and deceleration to change how hard it tries to reach its top speed. Finally, change a Mover’s Input Action to change how it reacts to logic. You can simply turn it on and off, or you can adjust its speed or strength on the fly!

120973791: With the Character Animation Tweaker, you gain precise control over a character’s animations. Let’s put one on a sackbot and take a peek. The first tweak you’ll see is the Override Default Rotation tweak. When this is set to yes, you’ll have complete control over how your sackbot is oriented in the world. Give it a go now and tweak the sackbot’s Pitch, Yaw, and Roll Angles. Amazing! Now enter the Choose Animation menu. You will only be able to choose animations associated with the type of bot being tweaked, so if you want to animate a Swoop sackbot or an Odd sock sackbot, be sure to change your sackbot’s form first. For now, let’s stick with a normal sackbot. On the left you’ll see animation categories. On the right, you’ll see the specific animations associated with those categories. Scroll through the lists until you find an animation you like. Once you’ve chosen an animation, you can play around with it. The Animation Speed tweak determines how fast the animation plays. The Animation Start and Animation End tweaks allow you to change how much of the full animation you’ll use. You can have it start and end at any point in the animation’s usual cycle. Of course, it’s easy to make this look very odd, so be sure your tweaks are having the desired effect. The Loop tweak determines whether an animation plays over and over again… or once. With the Reset if Inactive tweak set to Yes, the animation will start over from the beginning whenever it’s triggered. If you set it to No, it will start from wherever it left off – even if that means the very last frame. With the input action tweak, you can change how the animation plays based on logic. This can simply mean turning the animation on and off, making it play backwards, or something more complex like choosing specific frames in the animation with the positional option. For the next bit, let’s take a look at how animation tweakers behave on sequencers. Using sequencers, you can blend two animations together for smooth transitions or brand-new movements.  Change the way animations blend using the Animation Blend Action tweak. Animations can blend automatically, manually, or relative to their positions on the sequencer. Play around with it to get a feel for how it works! The actor name tweak is used in conjunction with a sackbot’s actor name so that you can animate sackbots from afar! Just set them up to match and any animation on the tweaker will apply to the sackbot as well. This is handy for keeping all the logic in your cutscenes in one place! Finally, you might have noticed the sequencer bar that progresses as the animation plays. Using this, you can trigger logic based on animation timing!

2043185607: When you want an object to chase something around, your best option is the Follower. It’s on the Gadgets page of your Tools Bag, so snatch one up and place it in the world with the action button. Look at it go! The object the Follower is on will move for Sackboy right away. Let’s adjust its behavior from the tweak menu – open it up with the menu button.  Adjust the Maximum Speed to make the Follower slower or faster. If you want the object to follow through the layers, you can adjust its In Out Speed as well – otherwise just keep it at zero. The Acceleration tweak determines how strong the Follower’s movement is – the stronger it is, the more it will fight against resistance to get to you! The Stabilizer tweak toggles whether the Follower takes a direct path or whether it can swerve around obstacles. You can adjust the range of the Follower’s awareness in the Trigger category. You can change its minimum and maximum radius, its angle range, and even its range in the layers. It’s also worth noting that you can give a Follower an infinite awareness radius by setting the Maximum Detection Range to less than zero! Change the Follower’s Input Action to change how it reacts to logic. You can simply turn it on and off, or you can use logic to adjust its strength or speed on the fly!  In the Behavior category, you can disable a Follower’s vertical movement with the Allow Up-Down Movement tweak. You can also completely reverse its behavior by setting it to Flee Rather Than Follow! If you’d rather the Follower chased after a Tag instead of Sackboy, use the Follow Tag or Character tweak and set up the appropriate Tag. Finally, if you only want the Follower to follow a specific character, choose one from your Characters page using the Character to Detect option. If you change your mind, just hit the Reset button!

1501931583: The Gameplay Tweaker changes the way characters move and interact with the world. They live on the Creatures & Characters page of your Tools Bag, so let’s take a look.  Once you’ve set one up, open its tweak menu with the menu button. The first category of tweaks controls a character’s movement. Select the type of movement you want to affect with the Movement Type tweak, and then change its speed using the Movement Modifier. Look how fast you can go! You can also change whether your character can grab or climb. You can enable or disable either one as you like! Next come the jump tweaks. The Jump Modifier tweak controls how high your character can jump, and the Air Steering tweak changes how much control a character has over its direction once it jumps.  In the Layers category, you can determine whether your character automatically changes layers in midair, whether it can manually change layers on the ground, and whether it can jump down from a higher layer to a lower one. You can set up any combination of these options that you want. The Affects tweak determines which characters receive these behaviors. If you want all of them to use them, set this to Affects All. The other options are useful when a Gameplay Tweaker is triggered by logic or placed onto a Broadcast Microchip or Sackbot! The Input Actions change how a Gameplay Tweaker reacts to logic. It can simply be turned on and off, but you can also use logic to alter a character’s movement speed or jump strength during gameplay!  Finally, the Vulnerability category lets you change what destroys your character. Just use the action button to toggle the vulnerabilities on and off. Now you’re ready to use the Gameplay Tweaker to customize your very own characters!

They’re found on the Gameplay page of your Tools Bag, so grab a pair of them now and place them in the world using the action button. Wormholes have two inputs: one to trigger them, and another to turn them on and off. Using the popit cursor, hook up one wormhole’s output to the other wormhole’s trigger input. Enter the second wormhole’s tweak menus using the menu button. You can make it static if you don’t want it to roll around. Then take a look at the Type tweak. By default, wormholes are set to be Entrances, so change this one to be an Exit instead. Now step in front of the Entrance wormhole and activate it. Pop! Out you come, right out of the Exit. If you don’t want your players to enter the wormholes manually, you can activate an Entrance wormhole with logic, instead. If you only want your lead player to teleport, just use the Entrance wormhole’s Players tweak. If you want players to be able to go back and forth between your wormholes, change both their types to Two-Way and hook them up to each other. Simple! Finally, if you don't want the wormholes to make their crazy noises, you can quiet them down with the wormhole's sounds tweak.

4224321692: Let’s take a look at some of the powerups available to the Sackboys and Sackgirls of LittleBigPlanet 3. They live in the Creatures & Characters page of your Tools Bag. First, take out the Hook Hat. With a Hook Hat on your head, you can rocket around on bendy rails! Attach to them by holding down the grab button and travel along them with the left stick. Let go of the grab button to drop down, or keep hold of it and press the action button to jump! Next, whip out some Boost Boots and try them on. To activate them, hold any direction with the left stick and press the grab button. You’ll be launched in that direction! You can even boost mid-jump for an instant change in direction! You can only use them once per jump, though; they’ll only reset once you touch the ground again… …unless they’ve been tweaked to recharge via a tag, too! With this option enabled, the Boost Boots will refresh whenever the player touches a certain tag.  While we’re here, it’s worth noting that each powerup also has the Can Be Dropped tweak, which either prevents or allows players removing the powerup once they’ve equipped it. Let’s quickly finish up by looking at the Powerup Remover – any player who touches one of these will have their powerup stripped away, whether it came from a pedestal or the sackpocket!

1301526801: Use Race Gates to add a fun high-speed challenge to your levels! There are two types: Start Gates and Finish Gates. Once a Start Gate is triggered, your players must reach a Finish Gate in the allotted time for big score bonuses! You can find them on the Gameplay page of your Tools Bag, so grab one of each and let’s examine how they work. Open up the Start Gate’s tweak menu using the menu button. Make it Static if you don’t want it to slide around, and then check out the Race Time tweak. Adjust this to change the duration of the race! The Ignore Controlinator tweak determines whether the Race Gate detects a character who is currently inside of a Controlinator. If you don’t want the actual Race Gate objects cluttering up your level, no worries! You can trigger them via logic instead.  You may have noticed that the Race Gates have outputs as well. The output on the Start Gate produces a signal while the race is counting down, and the output on the Finish Gate only produces a signal when your players successfully complete the race! Finally, there are also a set of Top-Down Start Gates and Finish Gates – these function identically to the normal ones. The difference is exclusively visual, so use either set as you please!

2611768982: Tags don’t do anything on their own, but they can be used as triggers and targets for many things. Why don’t we check them out? They’re on the Gadgets page of your Tools Bag.  You can place a tag on anything in the world, so slap one down and give it a tweak.  Change a tag’s colour to differentiate it from other tags. When something is set to react to red tags, for example, they won’t even notice blue or purple ones. For even more differentiation, you can give your tags labels. When a tag has a label, it will only trigger logic set up to notice both its colour and its label.  Let’s take a look at some of the logic that uses tags to better understand how they work. Find a tag sensor in your Tools Bag and set it down. A tag sensor is activated when the tag it’s hunting for is in its range. You can change which tag it’s looking for in the Tag Type category. Set it to match your tag and make sure it’s in range – there! It’s giving an output, and will continue doing so as long as it can see its tag. Next, take out an impact sensor and place it down. If you tweak an impact sensor to require a tag, it will only activate while its owner is touching something with the right tag.  Lastly, the physics tweaker can react to tags as well. With the Collisions: Tagged Objects tweak, a physics tweaker’s owner will only bump into things with the right tag. Conversely, the Collisions: Ignore Tagged Objects tweak will make its owner bump into everything except things with the right tag.  Now you’re ready to start using tags in all sorts of clever ways.

2334097138: The Goodies Bag is where all of your things live. Any stuff you can place in the world is stored there. Let’s access the popit and take a look. Press the menu button. Use the left stick to navigate to the Goodies Bag and open it up with the action button. The first page is the Materials Page, which contains the basic building blocks of LittleBigPlanet. Use the page buttons to turn to the Collected Objects page, where you’ll find all the fancy bits and pieces you discover during the adventure. Another page over and you’ll find the My Objects page, which is where your own personal creations wind up. And finally, the last page is Community Objects, where you can find anything given to you by other players. To take something out of your Goodies Bag, scroll to it with the directional buttons or the left stick and press the action button. Press the action button again to place it in the world, then back out of your popit with the back button. There it is! Amazing.

668000036: Now this piece of LittleBigPlanet technology is so clever, you could put it in a box and call it The Memorizer.  Oh. We kind of DID do that didn't we. Well, that proves my point. I think.  You can use The Memorizer to keep track of everything you do. Kind of like a diary, or an annoying little brother.  Let me show you how it works.  We're going to tell The Memorizer to remember the state of these lights at a precise moment in time.  First of all, you'll want to connect that bottom Toggle Switch to the 3rd input of the Memorizer.  Then, connect the 3rd output of the Memorizer to the bottom light panel on the right.  Now, as you can see, these 3 grab switches can be used to toggle the lights on the left off and on.  Perfect for creating the world's least flamboyant light show.  Now, if you connect the Remember button to the Memorizer's Trigger Input...  ...and then press the Remember button...  The Memorizer will remember that state, and put the lights on the right into exactly the same state.  Wonderful! And that is merely the first stop on our journey towards Amazingville.  Okay, now try grabbing the switches again to put the lights in a different state.  See how the lights on the right have stayed as they were?  That's because the Memorizer is still outputting the values you told it to remember.  A Memorizer is nothing if not obedient.  To make it forget these values, you need to reset the Memorizer.  Simply connect the Forget button to the Memorizer's Reset Input.  Jump on the button, and all of the remembered values will be forgotten.  Of course, the best way to learn something like this, is to have a good old-fashioned faff.  So feel free to play around with it as much as you like.

First off, let's learn the basics. Move your finger across the touch pad to move your paint cursor across the canvas. Push down on the touch pad to start painting! To resize your brush or spin it around, use two fingers and pinch, spread, or twist.  To switch between a normal brush and a scatter brush, press the menu button. If you want a new brush, press the grab button, gesture towards the one you like, and push in the touch pad. To choose a new color, press the back button and gesture towards the color you want, then push in the touch pad. If you want even more colors to choose from, hold down the R2 button while choosing. To erase a bit of your painting, hold down L1. Or you can use the undo and redo functions as usual! Press the options button to save your painting, quit painting altogether, or start anew. There are also other helpful options to browse. You can even pick another sticker as your background!  Finally, when you've saved a beautiful painting and you're ready to share it with the world, you can find it on your My Pictures page!

3671859530: The Physics Tweaker is used to alter the physical properties of an object: its weight and its solidity. You can find it on the Gadgets page of your Tools Bag. Fetch one now and place it on something in the world. Open its tweak menu. Right away, you can tweak its collisions – essentially, you can use the Physics Tweaker to change what can and can’t touch the object. By default, collisions are on. If you turn them off, the object will still be visible, but as far as other objects and characters are concerned, it may as well be empty space!  For further control over this effect, you can make your object only collide with tagged objects. Just select Tagged Objects and pick the appropriate tag. You can also set your object to ignore specific tags instead with the Ignore Tagged Objects option! If you want to make your object heavier or lighter, activate the Change Weight tweak, then select a new weight. Its untweaked weight is visible above these options, so adjust against this value however you like. Finally, if your object is part of a bigger object made up of many pieces, you can activate the Include Rigid Connections tweak to spread the effects of the Physics Tweaker to the entire thing!

2278587306: The Opacity Tweaker makes objects transparent or completely invisible! Take one out of the Gadgets page in your Tools Bag and let’s see how it works. Place it onto whatever you want to fade out using the action button. Open its tweak menu with the menu button. The first tweak you’ll see is the Opacity tweak, which you can change from a nice, fully visible 100% to a totally invisible 0%.  Be sure to check it out in preview mode to see how it’ll look to your players! Next, check out the Fade Time tweak. If your Opacity Tweaker is triggered by logic, this tweak represents how long it will take to fade from one opacity to the next. If you want an instant change, just keep it at zero! If the Opacity Tweaker is placed onto a light object, activating the Dim Lights tweak will fade out the brightness as well as the object itself. Use the Include Rigid Connections tweak to change whether the Opacity Tweaker also applies to objects the original object is glued to. Finally, change the Input Action to change how it reacts to logic – it can simply be turned on and off, or have its effect strength adjusted more directly.

4173464942: The Bolt is used to connect two objects in adjacent layers. It’s really simple stuff! First, position an object in front of a nice sturdy base. 1355788187: The Character Teleporter is used to warp players from one spot to another. Grab one from the Gameplay page of your Tools Bag and place it in the world with the action button. Be sure to wire a button to its input – the Character Teleporter won’t function without input from logic! Press the button and watch the magic as you pop out of the Character Teleporter. Amazing stuff, right? That’s the Character Teleporter at its simplest. Now open up its tweak menu with the menu button.  Use the Teleport All Players tweak to determine whether the Character Teleporter warps every player at once or just the one who activates it.  If the Character Teleporter has a Transition Time, it will hold a player in limbo for that length of time between being activated and spitting the player out. Finally, if your level is a Dynamic Thermometer Level, it might take a little time to teleport your players long distances. If that’s the case, you can allow or disallow the appearance of a load screen by adjusting the Show Loading Screen tweak!
